_comment: Ledger of recurring prose habits (constructions, gestures, paragraph/scene closers), the language-level counterpart to motifs.json. Nightly sessions read this before drafting and add entries after. Status: 'develop' = use only in a new form; 'rest' = do not use until rested_until chapter; 'watch' = fine in moderation. Saturday review prunes and logs counts.

constructions.pattern: 'the way [clause]' used as a trailing simile
constructions.example: the way you feel an old break in the weather before you feel the ache of it
constructions.note: Ch. 13 held at one clean use (Vantry's chimneys against Carrowgate's). Draft reached for it five more times during revision — Maria's hand-turning, the imbuing's kettle line, Edie's cable-measurement line, the cask line, the register-closing line — and every one was rewritten to a plain comparison ('like X') or cut outright rather than banked as a second or third use. Two chapters running at one; keep trimming rather than letting it climb back toward the ch. 07-09 level.

constructions.example: a thing to explain; a thing your body has quietly decided
constructions.note: Fourth chapter running at zero. Name the actual object or action — holding firmly now.

constructions.pattern: 'I have learned/found/never...' followed by a general rule
constructions.example: I have learned the exact weight a thing has to reach before it's worth the cost of saying it out loud
constructions.note: Came off rest at ch. 13 as scheduled and wasn't reached for even once — the building-watching material gave Lloyd plenty of behaviour (counting barrels, reporting flat) to substitute for narrated self-knowledge. Downgraded from 'rest' to 'watch' since the scheduled rest period has lapsed clean; keep treating a return to this pattern as a genuine lapse, not a scheduled allowance.

Ch. 13 held the established low-to-mid-20s range (19, just under it). Contrast rotated again: Lloyd's long sight-lines and dread-spirals against Vail's short, plain, warmly-delivered lines (relayed through Maria's retelling) and against Edie's flat procedural dialogue during the investigation montage — a three-way pairing, not the ch. 10-11 two-way one. Keep rotating the contrast partner rather than defaulting to any single one.

constructions.pattern: 'same as [clause]' used as a trailing comparison, the direct replacement for the rested the-way-simile
constructions.example: same as I run all of them back now
constructions.note: One clean, isolated use ('Edie making her own, same as always') after two chapters at zero. Still occasional rather than reached-for; no change in status warranted.

constructions.pattern: Lloyd narrates his own perception-management in filing/accounting/procedural language
constructions.example: filed and closed and not brought up again; I did the sum; running the frame back
constructions.note: Third chapter running clean. Ch. 13 gave the ledger-and-accounting register to Edie explicitly (a column that won't balance) and kept Lloyd's own self-management physical and visual (the gloved hand, running every private guess about the Church up against what Maria described) rather than procedural. Staying evolved away from.

constructions.pattern: a clause restated through its own negation for flat understatement — 'didn't X because there wasn't X to do', 'wasn't an answer that wasn't Y'
constructions.example: she didn't say anything useful, because there wasn't anything useful to say; I didn't have an answer that wasn't the same thing said back to her, worse
constructions.note: Third chapter running without it. Confirmed one-chapter cluster; still safe to use if it arises naturally, not a default.

constructions.pattern: a statement capped with a trailing 'which was/is [flat judgment]' clause
constructions.example: which was true, and also the kindest thing she could have said to her just then; which was as much of a question as Edie generally asks
constructions.note: Flagged last chapter as a four-use cluster needing development. Ch. 13 avoided the construction entirely rather than reusing it — draft originally reached for it twice (Edie putting her cord away, Lloyd's catalogue of worse guesses about the Church) and both were rewritten into separate declarative sentences instead. Treat as successfully evolved away from; a return to the bare trailing-'which' shape would be a real lapse now, not a continuation.

closers.pattern: paragraph or chapter ends on the narrator stating what he did not say, or what the scene means
closers.example: I said none of that. I hadn't said anything since the school wall and didn't start now.
closers.note: Ch. 12 closed on Edie's cord going still; ch. 13 closed on Edie knotting off a thread and a one-word decision spoken aloud ('Thursday'). Two chapters running on an object-plus-dialogue close instead.

closers.pattern: chapter ends on an image of something indifferent or inanimate personified as 'patient', waiting out time without hurry
closers.example: the night came down slow over the burnt manse... patient, working at the dark the way it works at everything, given enough time and no one to tell it to stop
closers.note: Spent at ch. 08-09 review; stayed spent through ch. 13. Do not return to 'patient' as a chapter-ending word.
